title: What is known about 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1LD0LC_1LA0LB_1RA1LF_---0LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LE_0RC0RA_1LD0LC_1LA0LB_1RA1LF_---0LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The machine is a binary counter: left of a periodic wall the tape reads as six-cell units holding one or two bits, and every three sweeps add one. When the counter is full, the carry rewrites the left part of the tape and the counting starts over. Rarely the carry runs to the left end (an S event): the old counter freezes into blocks and the wall, by then astronomically long, becomes the new counter. Lean proves every rule on the way from blank tape through the first S event, for all counter and wall lengths: no halt in the first 8p0+1 steps, p0 = 321,163,084,821,590,067,792,163 (a number with about 2.9·1023 digits). A trusted simulator gets through the next three S events without a halt. Each S event is a new, apparently random trial for halting, and the left part never settles into a pattern.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: Two sweeps that only touch the right end
claims.text: From the phase P right end 111011 (101011)^n 1 B>0 one sweep gives phase Q 101010 (111010)^n 111 B>0, and the next gives phase R 111110 (101110)^n 10111 B>0, in 16n+18 and 16n+26 steps, for every n and any tape left of them.

claims.title: One increment of the counter, for every carry
claims.text: Read the cells left of the wall in six-cell units, alternately X (111110 = 0, 111011 = 1) and Y (111011, 111010, 111111, 111110 = 0..3). Three sweeps from phase R add one to this mixed-radix (binary) number and one unit to the wall: X0 becomes X1, or a carry over a last X1 and j pairs Y3 X1 stops at a Y below 3 or at an X0. 48n+122, 60j+48n+154 (or +162 for Y1, +182 for an X stop) steps, for all j, n and any tape left of the counter.

claims.title: The increment as a program
claims.text: A program next on the list of units computes one increment and its number of steps; next_sound proves that the machine makes exactly that move whenever next answers, which it does unless the carry runs off the end of the list.

claims.title: From blank tape to the counter
claims.text: After 59,129 steps (sweep 149) the tape is the 34-cell left part 1 0 1^11 0 1^3 0 1 0 1^3 0 1 0 1 0 1^5 0, a 73-bit counter in 49 units, the edge unit and a wall of two units, by compiled evaluation of the list simulator.

claims.title: No halt in the first 2.4·10<sup>17</sup> steps
claims.text: next, run 100,000,000 times from there by compiled code without a gap: no halt in the first 240,000,021,742,916,313 steps.

claims.title: A full count, for any counter
claims.text: From any valid list of m units, the counter counts up to all ones in at least capP(m) − 1 − value steps (capP = number of values, 2·8<sup>k</sup> for 2k+1 units), for every m, every wall length and any tape left of it.

claims.title: The 17 carries into the left part, and the first S event
claims.text: With the counter all ones, the carry into the left part Lk gives the zero counter and Lk+1 (k = 0..16), for every even counter length and wall; the carry into L17 runs to the left end: the counter becomes the blocks of L1 = P (1^9 0 1 0)^j Q and a wall of 2p+2 units becomes the counter 1,3,0,3,0,… of 2p+3 units, for every j and p. Generated with bbtools.symtm by py/gen_left.py.

claims.title: The first six carries into L1
claims.text: With an odd all-ones counter, the first six carries into L1 only rewrite its last ten cells Q (Q<sub>0</sub> to Q<sub>6</sub>), for every counter length, wall and tape left of Q.

claims.title: Blank tape passes the first S event
claims.text: Chaining reach_s0, up, the 17 carries and s1: blank tape reaches L1 with 24 blocks, the counter ds1 p0 of 2p0+3 units and an empty wall, p0 = 321,163,084,821,590,067,792,163 (around step 1049); and then the configuration just before the seventh carry into L1. Kernel-checked apart from the native reach_s0.

claims.title: No halt in the first 8<sup>p0+1</sup> steps
claims.text: The new counter has 2·8<sup>p0+1</sup> values and six full counts precede the seventh carry, so the machine runs at least 8<sup>p0+1</sup> steps: a number with about 2.9·10<sup>23</sup> decimal digits.

claims.title: The second S event
claims.text: A memoized simulator of the carry map on the left part (the counter between carries is skipped) finds 2,266,846,918 carries into L1 before the second S event, without a halt. It gives a new irregular part P2 of 406 cells, p0+1 blocks and Q, and a new counter from the wall.

claims.title: Jumps, and the third and fourth S events
claims.text: The blocks are transparent: a carry crosses them in state C and returns in state A. A carry into P (a jump) changes P by a map J that depends on P only. J was checked against the direct run for the first 11 jumps with 300 blocks, and the result of the S event was checked to be independent of the number of blocks and of the cells right of them. Iterating J: 170,793,835 jumps on P2, no halt, then the third S event, giving P3 of 460 cells; 2,048,289,505 jumps on P3, no halt, then the fourth, giving P4 of 500 cells.

claims.title: Halting is possible at the left end
claims.text: The machine halts exactly when E reads a 1 with a 0 on its left, and this can happen when a carry arrives at the left end: for the synthetic left part P B^2 Q with an even counter it halts after 1,129 carries. From blank tape all counters after S1 have odd length.
claims.where: README, section Where it could halt

claims.title: No closed family
claims.text: The irregular part is new at each level (28, 406, 460, 500 cells) and the number of jumps until the next S event is irregular (about 2.3·10<sup>9</sup> carries, then 1.7·10<sup>8</sup> and 2.0·10<sup>9</sup> jumps). Each S event looks like a fresh random trial for halting, and the time between them grows like a tower; no invariant family is in sight.
claims.where: README, section Why it does not close

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Deciding it needs either the outcome of every future S event (each computable by iterating J on a few hundred cells, but with ever more jumps), or a reason why the left end never shows E over a 1 next to a 0.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet, but we know what it does: it counts in binary, and every time the counter fills up the carry scribbles on the far left of the tape. Very rarely the carry reaches the left end; then the whole counter freezes into the left part and the wall, by then unimaginably long, becomes a new counter. Lean follows the machine through the first of these events, past 8<sup>p0+1</sup> steps with p0 ≈ 3.2·10<sup>23</sup>. What happens at the later ones looks random.

facts.text: Increments, full counts and left-end events up to the second level, for all counter and wall lengths.
Simulated through the second, third and fourth left-end events without a halt.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.488).
After 109 steps the tape spans 39,053 cells (50 left of the start, 28,650 right), with a density of 1s of 0.668.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: What the tape is made of
html: The right part of the tape is a wall: the six cells 010111 over and over, two cells longer after every trip of the head. Left of the wall, cut the tape into pieces of six cells, starting at the wall. Each piece, a unit, is one of a handful of words, and the units take turns being of two kinds:

X unit (1 bit)cellsY unit (2 bits)cells
X0111110Y0111011
X1111011Y1111010
Y2111111
Y3111110

Nearest the wall is an X unit (bit 0), then a Y unit (bits 1 and 2), then X (bit 3), Y (bits 4 and 5), and so on: together a binary number. Between the counter and the wall sits one edge unit, 111110 once every three trips. Far to the left is a short irregular piece that is not made of units: the left part.

sections.heading: Three trips, one increment
html: Two of every three trips are short: the head walks left over the wall, turns inside the edge unit, and walks back. Each adds two cells to the wall and changes nothing else. The third trip goes deeper: it crosses every unit that holds its maximum (X1 or Y3), turns at the first unit that does not, and on the way back rewrites the crossed units to their minimum. That is exactly adding one, with a carry.

The wall grows by one unit per increment, so the k-th increment takes about 48k steps: the run is quadratic and the tape grows like the square root of the time.

sections.heading: From blank tape
html: The first 145 trips are a scramble in which a small counter grows against the left end. From step 59,129 on the tape is a 28-cell left part L0, a counter of 50 units and the wall (reach_s0, checked by compiled Lean). The counter is 8.4·1019 increments from full; then the carry reaches the left part for the first time, around step 1041.

sections.heading: Counters inside counters
html: When the counter is all ones, the next carry has nowhere to go inside it. It runs on into the left part and rewrites a few of its cells, and the counter starts again from zero, now with a longer wall. Proved in Lean: from blank tape this happens 17 times, each time rewriting the left part Lk into Lk+1 by a rule that holds for every counter length and wall length.

The 18th carry does something new: it runs all the way to the left end of the tape. Call this an S event. The old counter is frozen into identical blocks 1^9 0 1 0, and the wall, which by then has 2·p0+2 units with p0 = 321,163,084,821,590,067,792,163, becomes the new counter.

The new counter has 2·8p0+1 values, so the time to the next carry into the left part is beyond astronomical. Each carry either stays near the right end of the blocks or makes a jump: it crosses the blocks without changing them and rewrites the irregular piece P on the far left by a map J that depends on P alone. When a jump comes back in the wrong state (B instead of A) it is the next S event, and the whole picture repeats one level up with a new P.

P never settles: 28, 406, 460, 500 cells of what looks like noise, and J scrambles it. That is why the question stays open: every S event is a new roll of the dice for a halt.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The missing transition is F reading 0, and F is entered only from E reading 1, which steps left. So the machine halts exactly when E reads a 1 with a 0 on its left. In every proved rule F lands on a 1. The place where it could fail is the left end of the tape, at an S event: what state the carry arrives in there depends on the irregular cells of P. For a made-up left part (P B^2 Q with an even-length counter) the machine does halt, after 1,129 carries; the configurations reached from blank tape have so far always been safe.

sections.heading: What is proved
html: Lean, kernel. The two short trips and the five kinds of three-trip increment, for every wall length and carry length (lean/Rules.lean); the increment as a program on the units (next_sound, lean/Counter.lean); a full count of a counter of any length (up, lean/Count.lean); the 17 carries into the left part, the first S event and the first six carries into L1, for all counter and wall lengths (fe, s1, fo, lean/Left.lean).

Lean, kernel on top of one native_decide. Blank tape reaches the first S event and goes on to the seventh carry into L1: no halt in the first 8p0+1 steps (no_halt_early, lean/Frontier.lean), where only the first 59,129 steps (reach_s0) use compiled evaluation.
Trusted computation. The second S event after 2,266,846,918 carries into L1, the third after 170,793,835 jumps into P2 and the fourth after 2,048,289,505 jumps into P3, none halting (py/accel/).

Open. All later S events. Each one is a finite computation on a few hundred cells, but the number of jumps before it is large and unpredictable, and nothing suggests a pattern that a proof could follow.

family: counter whose overflows freeze into a self-similar, chaotic left end
summary: A binary counter in six-cell units whose overflows rewrite an irregular left part; rarely an overflow reaches the left end, the old counter freezes into blocks and the wall becomes a far longer counter. Lean proves the run through the first such event (no halt in the first 8^(p0+1) steps, p0 about 3.2e23); the next three are computed, and the left part behaves chaotically, so the question stays open.
